items.text: Understand what virtualization is and why it was invented (resource contention problem)
Explain the role of a hypervisor and name three hypervisor tools
Describe the key differences between a VM and a container (OS, size, startup time, resource allocation)
Explain what containerization is and what problem it solves
Define microservices architecture and explain why containers suit it
Explain what CI/CD stands for and the purpose of each stage in a CI pipeline
Describe the Git workflow: working directory → staging → local repo → remote repo
Write a basic Dockerfile with FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN, and CMD instructions
Build a Docker image using docker build and tag it correctly
Run a container with docker run including port mapping (-p flag)
Use docker ps, docker stop, docker rm, and docker rmi commands
Create a feature branch, commit changes, push to GitHub, and raise a Pull Request
Install Docker on an EC2 instance and deploy a containerized web application
Identify whether a scenario calls for a VM or a container and justify the choice
Name the CI pipeline stages in order and the tool associated with each stage
Distinguish between Continuous Delivery (manual prod approval) and Continuous Deployment (fully automatic)
Explain the Docker workflow: Dockerfile → Image → Registry → Container
Name AWS-native equivalents for GitHub (CodeCommit), Docker Hub (ECR), Jenkins (CodeBuild), and Kubernetes (EKS)
Identify what SonarQube, JUnit, Maven, and JaCoCo each do in a CI pipeline
Answer STAR-format behavioral interview questions about cloud engineering challenges
